data.why: The app takes plain-language text input and queries live public literature APIs (PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex); it has no file upload and keeps its own SQLite note store (notebook.db) created automatically at startup.

goals: Describe a research focus in plain language and get consolidated results from PubMed, Europe PMC, and OpenAlex in one search
Inspect the auto-generated Boolean queries sent to each database to verify the search strategy before relying on it
Narrow a search to a single database (e.g., PubMed only) when scoping a review to biomedical literature
Save a named research note that records the query, sources, and results for later reference
Export the consolidated search results, including titles, authors, abstracts and links, as a Word document for a literature review

review.summary: The tree describes the README's purpose accurately: plain-language input becomes a Boolean query for each database, PubMed, Europe PMC and OpenAlex are searched together, the results come back as one list, and they can be saved and exported to Word. Its phases, tasks and most of its evidence hold up. Before filing it needs the query-refinement task, correct export evidence (the downloaded files instead of screens/018 and 029), an accurate term count in f1, and f4 split into two features.
